For attainment, rescale the fine normals to unit length, choose convergent normals and coordinatewise extended-real limits of the finitely many level thresholds. At divergent levels the indicator tends to zero; at finite thresholds its limsup is bounded by the limiting hyperplane indicator.

The threshold vector on the surviving levels stays in the closed linear image of the coarse coefficients and intercept. One coupled hyperplane realizes the finite limits; any extra mass it captures only helps the reverse Fatou estimate. If no level survives the limiting mass is zero, so every hyperplane attains the zero supremum. The a=0 case is the same compactness argument on the common threshold.

Pullback makes the fine coefficient A^T b, nonzero by invertibility. The inverse is again triangular in the base and fine coordinates. This is exact invariance for the pushed-forward law, even with level-dependent fine coset offsets.

The tube is full-dimensional when J≥2, epsilon>0 and K has interior. At coarse integer j, the strip of fine width 2 epsilon<1 contains just fine integer j. The J equal fibers yield eta_u=1/J and eta_c=1; the original exact arithmetic verifier confirmed the census and ratio for J=2 through 30.

overlap.comparison: Uses a bounded count of coarse levels to select one actual retained fiber hyperplane in a depth estimate, with section-volume and rank hypotheses. It has no comparison of the coupled and uncoupled hyperplane families under arbitrary finite measures or shear invariance.

Vertical-preserving maps preserve a single-level fine family. The coarse-to-fine shear here acts across finitely many coarse levels and preserves the coupled hyperplanes under pushforward, with a sharp quantitative comparison to the uncoupled family.
